rounds.text: Supreme Power Equipment Ltd exhibits exceptional fundamental strength and momentum, underscored by a rules-based screen scoring 98 out of 100 with high confidence [E53]. This performance is driven by extraordinary top-line expansion, highlighted by 46% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E15], 3-year compounded sales growth of 22% [E14], and a massive +133% year-over-year sales surge [E54]. Profitability metrics are equally robust, delivering a 20.73% ROCE and 18.72% ROE that significantly outpace sector benchmarks of 12.88% and 11.25% respectively [E10, E9]. Furthermore, operational efficiency has dramatically improved, with debtor days dropping from 139 to 94.1 days [E50] and working capital requirements shrinking from 94.0 days to 39.1 days [E51]. Order book visibility remains exceptional at over INR565.80 crores [E76], backed by management guidance for full-year FY27 revenue between INR300 crores and INR350 crores [E63] and strong secular demand for power infrastructure over the next 8 to 10 years [E67]. Conceded: operating margins have compressed by 3 percentage points to 17% in TTM compared to three years earlier [E21], free cash flow stood at negative Rs 32 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27], and institutional holdings have experienced significant declines since Dec 2023 [E33, E34].

Conceded: [E36]. Despite reported growth metrics, the fundamental structure of Supreme Power Equipment carries stark operational vulnerabilities and cash generation disconnects that undermine its valuation multiples. Operating margins have eroded continuously, dropping by 3 percentage points from 20% to 17% both on a TTM basis and in the September 2026 quarter, with the yearly trend explicitly categorized as decreasing over the last four years [E21, E22, E23]. This margin compression occurs alongside a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -32 crore in March 2026, directly contrasting with reported net profits [E27]. Furthermore, leverage is climbing as borrowings expanded to Rs 57 crore by September 2026 compared to Rs 50 crore a year prior [E30], while the current ratio sits at a thin buffer of 1.28x [E29]. Institutional confidence has completely collapsed, evidenced by foreign institutional holdings plunging from 9.21% in December 2023 to just 0.75% and domestic institutional holdings crashing from 11.31% to 0.23% over the same period [E33, E34]. Finally, the equity provides zero dividend yield [E4], and shareholders face an exceptionally high annualised volatility of 71.0% alongside a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -74.2% [E44, E45].

Conceded: [E21, E22, E23, E27]. While operating margins have compressed by three percentage points and free cash flow landed at negative Rs 32 crore [E27], operating cash flow itself was a robust Rs 26 crore with a healthy cash conversion ratio of 1.24x, meaning profits are backed by actual cash collection [E25, E26]. The modest increase in borrowings to Rs 57 crore is entirely manageable against a strong market capitalisation of Rs 610 crore [E3, E30]. The dramatic exit of historical institutional holdings is contradicted by current positive money flow signals showing an uptick in institutional accumulation [E33, E34, E35]. Furthermore, the lack of a dividend yield [E4] is standard for a high-growth manufacturer aggressively compounding sales at 46% in the trailing twelve months and funding capacity expansion at the newly inaugurated Kannur facility [E15, E70]. Finally, historical volatility and drawdowns [E44, E45] overlook the present technical strength of the stock trading above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 [E41, E42].

Conceded: [E25, E26]. The bull points to operating cash flow of Rs 26 crore and a 1.24x cash conversion ratio, but ignores the severe negative free cash flow of Rs -32 crore [E27] and rising borrowings touching Rs 57 crore [E30], which directly undermine the claim of financial health. While the bull downplays the three percentage point compression in operating margins [E21, E22], this negative trend has persisted continuously over four years [E23] and exposes the vulnerability of relying on raw material price variation clauses that suffer from dangerous timing lags [E81]. The bull dismisses historical institutional exits, yet the empirical drop from 9.21% down to 0.75% for foreign institutions and from 11.31% down to 0.23% for domestic institutions represents an overwhelming institutional abandonment [E33, E34] that a minor fractional quarterly flow signal [E35] cannot repair. Finally, the total absence of a dividend yield [E4] combined with a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of 74.2% [E44] and 71% annualized volatility [E45] means ordinary shareholders bear immense risk without any cash return, regardless of moving average technical positioning [E41].

Conceded: [E27]. The severe negative free cash flow of Rs -32 crore and rising borrowings touching Rs 57 crore [E30] are natural companions to active capital deployment, underscored by a steady ₹32 crore in capital work-in-progress [E31] and the successful ramp-up of the Kannur facility [E70] toward an 80% utilization target next year [E83]. Conceded: [E21, E22, E23]. While operating margins experienced a three percentage point compression over four years, management actively safeguards profitability through price variation clauses covering 70% to 75% of the order book [E73], successfully anchoring projected PAT margins between 9% and 12% [E65] on a robust order book exceeding ₹565.80 crores [E76]. Conceded: [E33, E34]. The exit of prior institutional holders is thoroughly outweighed by positive institutional money flow showing a holding increase [E35], paired with an elite rules-based screen score of 98 out of 100 [E53]. Conceded: [E4, E44, E45]. The total lack of dividend yield and high historical volatility are the necessary trade-offs for a hyper-growth capital goods business delivering 46% TTM sales growth [E15] and securing ₹209.24 crores in new orders during H1 FY27 alone [E75].

Conceded: [E27]. The bull's dismissal of a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -32 crore [E27] and rising borrowings touching Rs 57 crore [E30] overlooks the tangible balance sheet strain, particularly when current assets provide only an adequate but thin buffer with a current ratio of 1.28x [E29]. Conceded: [E21, E22, E23]. While the bull points to price variation clauses covering 70% to 75% of the order book [E73], this protection is clearly imperfect, as evidenced by a multi-year decreasing trend in operating margins [E23] and a persistent three percentage point compression down to 17% [E21, E22] driven by timing differences between raw material cost spikes in inputs like CRGO steel and corresponding price adjustments [E81]. Conceded: [E33, E34]. The bull's reliance on positive institutional money flow [E35] fails to explain the dramatic exodus of institutional capital, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings collapsing from 9.21% and 11.31% down to a negligible 0.75% and 0.23% respectively [E33, E34]. Furthermore, the total absence of a dividend yield [E4] combined with an annualized volatility of 71.0% and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -74.2% [E44, E45] reveals that investors shoulder immense downside risk without any cash return while management defers shareholder payouts.

evidence.quote: And based on the order book, the margin can be maintained between -- the PAT margin can be maintained between 9% to 12%.

evidence.quote: Yes. Actually, now the demand environment is very good and the sector is also very good. Since the Union Government and the State Governments showing much interest in expanding the transmission network, the demand is very high.

evidence.quote: As per market information, next 8 to 10 years, there will be good demand for this power sector.

evidence.quote: The strong growth reflects healthy execution of our order book and continued demand across our key markets.

evidence.quote: Next year, we have to think and plan about that.

evidence.quote: The ramp-up of our newly inaugurated Kannur facility is progressing well, with production and capacity utilisation scaling up as planned.

Total Capacity

evidence.fact: Management noted pressure from higher prices of key inputs, particularly CRGO steel and transformer oil.
evidence.quote: During the period, we have seen pressure from higher prices of key inputs, particularly CRGO steel and transformer oil.

evidence.fact: Management stated that around 70% to 75% of the order book is covered under price variation clauses.
evidence.quote: Importantly, around 70% to 75% of our order book is covered under price variation clauses, which provides a degree of protection against volatility in key raw material prices.

evidence.fact: Management stated that higher overheads and skilled manpower requirements for power transformers absorb the margin differential versus distribution transformers.
evidence.quote: Actually, for power transformers, the margin is slightly higher than the distribution transformer. But at the same time, it is absorbed by the overheads. So, it needs skilled manpower, so we have to deploy experienced people. So, this 0.5% or 1% margin is absorbed by the -- so this margin will maintain and it will sustain.

evidence.fact: Supreme Power secured 11 orders aggregating INR209.24 crores with execution timelines ranging between 7 and 17 months in H1 FY27.
evidence.quote: During H1 FY27, we secured 11 orders aggregating INR209.24 crores, with execution timelines ranging between 7 months and 17 months.

evidence.fact: The company's current order book stands at over INR565.80 crores.
evidence.quote: Our current order book stands at over INR565.80 crores, providing strong execution visibility for the coming periods.

evidence.fact: Out of the total order book of INR565 crores, distribution is around 16% to 17%, power transformer is around 75% to 78%, and inverter duty transformers are around 5%.
evidence.quote: Out of this INR565 crores, distribution is around 16% to 17%, that is less than INR95 crores. And power transformer is around INR440 crores that comes around 78% -- 75% to 78%. And inverter duty transformers is around INR30 crores, that comes 5% of the total order book.

evidence.fact: Management stated that private customers provide advance payments, and repeat customers receive credit for 45 to 60 days.
evidence.quote: Private, some customers, we are getting advance. Most of the customers we get 10% to 30% advance. And before dispatch, we use to get 90% and balance 5% to 10% will be after commissioning. And for repeat customers, we used to give credit for 45 days to 60 days.

evidence.fact: Government payments are received within 60 to 90 days.
evidence.quote: From the government, we get payments in 60 to 90 days.

evidence.quote: So for this year, there is no requirement for equity dilution.

evidence.quote: These movements can impact margins, especially where there is a timing difference between increase in input costs and the corresponding adjustment under the price variation clause.

evidence.quote: And though there was a geopolitical issues were there due to that, the price rise of the raw materials are being absorbed because of this price variation clause, which we get from our buyers.
